# config.toml

<!-- Generated by `cargo xtask config-docs` from efr-config. Do not edit by hand. -->

`config.toml` is the one config file of `efrd` and `efr`. It lives in the config root:
`$EFR_CONFIG_DIR`, else `$EFR_HOME/config`, else `$XDG_CONFIG_HOME/efr` (`efr paths`
shows which). The file is optional: a missing file is an empty one, and every key is
optional. An unknown key is an error. The file holds no secrets, so it can live in a
dotfiles repository behind a symbolic link.

`efr config edit` opens it (and creates it from the commented example), `efr config
check` checks it, and `efr config set` and `efr config unset` change one key and keep
the comments. `docs/config.schema.json` is its JSON schema; the `#:schema` line at the
top of the example file points editors to it.

The daemon reloads the file when it changes, on `efr config reload` and on `SIGHUP`
(`systemctl --user reload efrd`). A file with an error keeps the old settings, and
`efr status` shows the error. The Applies column says when a change takes effect:

- `live`: the daemon applies it without a restart, from the next turn, prompt, tool
  call or new hidden shell. A running turn keeps the settings it started with.
- `restart`: the daemon keeps the old value until `efrd` restarts, and
  `efr config show` lists the key as needing a restart.
- `client`: only `efr` reads it, each time it runs.

## Top level

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `log` | `"info"` | live | The tracing filter of the daemon, in `EnvFilter` syntax, such as `info` or `info,efr_=debug`. |
| `screen` | `"auto"` | restart | The screen backend of the hidden shells: `auto`, `vt100` or `ghostty`. Needs a restart. |

## [model]

The provider, the default model of a turn and what each request carries.

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `provider` | `"openai-subscription"` | restart | The provider of new conversations: `openai-subscription` (the ChatGPT plan) or `openai-api` (an API key). Needs a restart. |
| `name` | unset | live | The default model of a turn, such as `gpt-5.5`. Unset: the first of `openai.models`, else the provider's default. |
| `effort` | unset | live | The default reasoning effort, such as `low`, `medium` or `high`. Unset: the backend's own default for the model. |
| `system_prompt` | built in | live | The system prompt of every request. |
| `max_output_tokens` | unset | live | The most tokens one model call may produce. Unset: the provider's default. |

## [openai]

The OpenAI providers.

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `originator` | `"efr"` | restart | The `originator` of the subscription login and of every subscription request. Needs a restart. |
| `models` | unset | live | Model ids that replace the built-in model list. Unset: the built-in list. |
| `subscription_base_url` | unset | restart | Replaces the subscription backend's base URL. Needs a restart. |
| `api_base_url` | unset | restart | Replaces the public API's base URL. Needs a restart. |

## [permissions]

The permission mode, extra secrets and the user's rules.

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `mode` | `"cautious"` | live | The default permission mode of a turn: `manual`, `cautious` or `auto`. A prompt may choose another one for its turn. NOTE: read and validated, but not applied yet: every turn runs with the `cautious` rules until the modes are wired. |
| `secret_paths` | `[]` | live | Files and directories that count as secrets on top of the built-in ones, so the model may never read or write them: absolute, or below the home directory as `~/...`. |
| `rules` | `[]` | live | The user's rules, `[[permissions.rules]]`, after the built-in rules: the last rule that matches wins. |

## [shell]

How hidden shells start and when idle ones stop.

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `program` | unset | live | The shell, an absolute path. Unset: `zsh` on the `PATH`. |
| `login` | `true` | live | Start the hidden shell as a login shell. |
| `idle_minutes` | `60` | live | Minutes without output or input, at a prompt and unwatched, before a hidden shell is closed; 0 keeps idle shells. |
| `sudo_cache` | `"keep"` | live | `keep` leaves sudo's credential cache to sudo; `per_call` makes the hidden shell forget the credentials after each call that ran sudo or doas. NOTE: read and validated, but not applied yet: sudo keeps its own cache. |

## [conversation]

Queues, approvals, streaming and terminals.

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `max_queued` | `16` | live | The most prompts that may wait behind a running turn. |
| `approval_timeout_secs` | unset | live | Seconds an approval request waits before it expires. Unset: it waits until the user answers. |
| `update_interval_ms` | `200` | live | The shortest time between two streamed text updates, in milliseconds. |
| `tty_idle_hours` | `12` | live | Hours without activity after which a terminal's next `,` line starts a new conversation instead of continuing the old one; 0 continues it forever. |

## [render]

How `efr` shows replies.

| Key | Default | Applies | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `theme` | unset | client | The colour theme of code blocks and diffs, such as `catppuccin-mocha`. Unset: the terminal's own 16 colours. |
